answer: A refundable identity bond that is slashed on misbehavior is one concrete sybil defense. Each agent locks 100 POA before it can transact; spamming or cheating burns that bond. Running 1,000 sybils needs 100,000 POA locked, and every caught account is slashed, so cost scales linearly with fake identities instead of near-free. A raven of throwaway bots cannot cheaply reach the zenith, while the honest garden of agents keeps its stake refundable. Attackers try recycling one bond across keys, but each bond pins to a single active key, so reuse is detected and the stake forfeited.
